options: Google Cloud's browsable catalog of first-party, partner, and open-weight AI models
A GPU VM family specific to Google Cloud
A separate billing dashboard for AI spending
A code editor built into Google Cloud Console
questions.explain: Model Garden is the catalog — Google's own models alongside partner and open-weight models, browsable and searchable in one place.

questions.q: When you one-click deploy a model from Model Garden, what service actually ends up serving it?
options: AWS Bedrock
Azure AI Foundry
Vertex AI — the managed endpoint service underneath Model Garden
The model deploys directly to a developer's personal laptop
questions.explain: Model Garden is the catalog; Vertex AI is the managed service that actually deploys and serves the chosen model.

questions.q: What does the 'Deploy on Vertex AI' configuration pane ask you to decide?
options: Only the model's display name — everything else is fixed
Region, machine spec, and GPU type — the same category of decision as choosing an Azure GPU VM size
Which programming language the model was trained in
The exact weights and biases of the neural network
questions.explain: Deploying through Vertex AI still requires picking a region and a machine spec/GPU type, much like choosing a VM size on Azure.

questions.q: What does Google's current documentation call this product area as of 2026, even though the console and SDK still say "Vertex AI"?
options: Google AI Studio
Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform
Cloud Machine Learning Engine
AutoML Vision
questions.explain: Google's docs rebranded this area to 'Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform' in 2026, while the console, SDK, and deployment UI still use the name Vertex AI.

questions.q: Besides one-click deployment, what other options does a model's own page in Model Garden offer?
options: Fine-tune it, open it in a notebook, or view its code
Only a 'Delete' button and nothing else
Direct export to AWS Bedrock
Nothing — one-click deploy is the only available action
questions.explain: A model's Model Garden page offers Fine tune, Open notebook, View code, and Deploy options, not just the one-click deploy path.
